svg.title: Treasury sign-in and device registration
svg.desc: Establish a revocable server session, then make an ACS web endpoint reachable. Sign-in alone does not verify a session. Source-verified EntraGuard flow. Official Microsoft architecture icons.

text.tspan: Establish a revocable server session, then make an ACS web endpoint reachable. Sign-in alone does not verify a session.
NUMBERED INTERACTIONS · time runs downward · dashed = response / conditional interaction (not every branch runs)
Numbers match the interaction on the left.
01 MSAL signs in the user and requests an EntraGuard API access
02 The access token is for the backend API. An ID token is not
03 The BFF checks same origin and a Bearer header before
04 Validate the API token. Derive tenant, object ID and roles
05 Store a credential hash and role snapshot. Expiry is capped at
06 Return the session credential to the BFF; a previous cookie
07 Set SameSite=Lax and Secure in production. Return signedIn,
08 For an ACS web endpoint, POST /api/acs/token with deviceKind
09 The BFF translates its cookie into a server-session header.
10 Register or reuse the device kind for this owner/session;
never trust a supplied owner ID.
11 Create an ACS identity if needed, then issue a scoped VoIP
12 Return the ACS identity and token through the BFF. The web
13 Heartbeat ownership/session is checked; LastSeen must be
Teams does not use this ACS web-device registration path; it relies on Teams endpoints and federation.
Device registration and sign-in do not issue a Treasury verification grant. Continue with diagrams 03 and 04.
Source/configuration review · 20 September 2026 · not a live deployment audit · original Microsoft icons; see asset credits and source references in the companion guide.
